To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) glucose utilization by adipose tissue from patients with adult-onset diabetes is defective; and (2) this defect is also present in patients who may be predisposed to develop diabetes, such as patients with Cushing’s syndrome or with obesity.

the defect of glucose utilization seen in the adipose tissue of patients with adult-onset diabetes mellitus can be found in the tissue of patients predisposed to diabetes, such as obese patients and patients with latent diabetes.
glucose utilization by adipose tissue from diabetic patients is impaired.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the metabolism of glucose and fatty acids in the adipose tissue of man and its possible relationship to diabetes mellitus.
the study of the biochemical basis of the development of adult diabetes.
the role of adipose tissue in the pathogenesis of diabetes and the predisposing factors to its development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this investigation provide evidence that glucose utilization by adipose tissue of the adult human diabetic is defective.

adipose tissue from diabetic patients, latent diabetics and patients with Cushing8s disease, obesity, and pregnancy showed a pattern of glucose utilization more like that of diabetic adipose tissue than that of normal adipose tissue.
a defect of glucose utilization is present in adipose tissue from a group of adult diabeties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the defect of glucose utilization found in adipose tissue in adult diabetics is also present in adipose tissue from obese patients and in some patients who are predisposed to develop diabetes.

the defect in glucose utilization in adipocytes from adult diabeti cs and in some conditions predisposing to diabetes is due to a failure of the tissue to respond to glucose, glucose 1-phosphate or l-glycerol-3-phosphate with increased conversion of glucose into phosphate esters.

in the adult diabetics, Cushing9s patients, latent diabetics and obese patients who showed a diabetic pattern, glucose phosphorylation and glucose oxidation were slower than in paired controls and this was accompanied by a slower conversion of glucose into fatty acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diabetic state is associated with impaired glucose utilization in adipocytes.
the adipose tissue from diabetic patients and those who are predisposed to diabetes have a defect in glucose metabolism which can be detected in vitro.
adipose tissue from adult diabeties has a defect of glucose utilization, and this may predispose to the development of the disease.
